canonical_title: The Selected Letters of Philip K. Dick: 1980-1982
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: The final Underwood-Miller volume, covering 1980 to PKD's death in March 1982, the years of the VALIS trilogy, his fullest late statements on 2-3-74, and his last correspondence before the fatal stroke.
page_summary:
This volume gathers Philip K. Dick's correspondence from 1980 until his death in March 1982, the last phase of his life and work. These are the years of the VALIS trilogy, VALIS, The Divine Invasion, and The Transmigration of Timothy Archer, and the letters track PKD working out the novels' theology while continuing to revise his understanding of the 1974 events in the Exegesis.

The correspondence carries his late exchanges with agents, scholars, and friends, his plans for further novels, and his reflections on his career as recognition finally began to reach him. It also includes his response to the coming Blade Runner adaptation. The volume ends where his life did, with the stroke that killed him at fifty-three.

As the closing volume of the Selected Letters, it is the primary correspondence source for PKD's final period and the summation of his religious thought.
